quests.title: First Light
quests.description: Help Stella diagnose and power her repaired electrical relic.

quests.title: String Them Together
quests.description: Help Stella connect the circuit relics.

quests.title: Out of Alignment
quests.description: Help Cinna Cirra align the orientation objects and learn Vis.

quests.title: Cold Feet, Warm Idea
quests.description: Help Cinna Cirra trigger the trial traps in order and learn Glaciate.

quests.title: Patch Notes
quests.description: Help Orio optimise the rotating mechanism and learn Rotara.

quests.title: Something Borrowed
quests.description: Use Lost Echoes to help Katrina recover a keepsake.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: You came at the right time. My relic should store a charge and pass it on, but the prototype is refusing to cooperate.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: Thank you. Start with the practical fault: trace where the charge stops, then restore the broken link. Once the relic is sound, I’ll need Ampere to wake it.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: Follow the path from the source to the receiver. A dark link means the charge cannot cross it; repair that before casting Ampere at the relic.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: It works. I had planned every measurement and still forgot to ask someone to look at the obvious thing. Maybe magical engineering needs a little less perfection and a little more collaboration.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: The first relic survived my repairs. The next board is worse: every special circuit relic must reach the right partner, and my plan is… technically elegant but not yet working.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: Use Weave to join compatible endpoints. Keep the route readable and make sure each connection reaches its intended relic; I refuse to call a tangled board finished.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: Check the endpoint symbols before you weave. If a line crosses a blocked space or leaves a relic stranded, back up and try the neighbouring route.

nodes.speaker: Stella
nodes.text: A clean circuit, and I accepted help before rebuilding the whole thing. That is progress on both assignments.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: I registered for orientation duty because it sounded welcoming. It is apparently for students who already know how half these objects work.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: I overheard that Vis can align what is out of place. Let’s compare each object with its matching marker, then reposition it carefully instead of guessing.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: Look for the face or mark that should meet the target. Align one object at a time; the terrace audience is not part of the puzzle.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: Thank you. I thought being prepared meant already knowing everything. Asking for help feels much more useful.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: There is one more orientation trial. The traps must trigger in order, and I would prefer not to discover the wrong order with my feet.

choices.text: Let’s find a safe way through.
What do we know so far?

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: Glaciate should let us freeze the ground and slide. We need the required sequence, a clear stopping boundary, and a walking lane back if a cast carries us too far.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: Read the numbered or marked triggers before sliding. Start from the safe edge, commit to one movement, and stop at the boundary before choosing the next trap.

nodes.speaker: Cinna Cirra
nodes.text: Cold feet, warm idea. I was frightened of making a mistake, but the sequence became manageable once we observed it together.

nodes.speaker: Orio
nodes.text: Welcome to the mechanism glade. I’m one turn away from a perfect optimisation, which is exactly why I’m not touching it again until the sequence is right.

nodes.speaker: Orio
nodes.text: Think of it like Spellio turns: each rotation changes what the next component can do. Rotara lets you rotate a component; try a configuration, observe the result, and keep notes.

nodes.speaker: Orio
nodes.text: Start with the component that receives the output, then reason backwards through the turn order. If one rotation fixes a neighbour but breaks the chain, that is useful information.

nodes.speaker: Orio
nodes.text: Perfect enough, and quicker than rebuilding it in my head. Turns out practical checks are a feature, not a patch note.

nodes.speaker: Katrina
nodes.text: I’m looking for something. It is hardly a crisis, so please don’t make that face. I can replace it if I must.

nodes.speaker: Katrina
nodes.text: Lost Echoes should reveal traces where an item has been separated from its owner. Start where I last searched, then follow the points of interest toward the planting alcove.

nodes.speaker: Katrina
nodes.text: Use Lost Echoes near the garden walk and follow the revealed points in order. If the trail ends, return to the last place where the item could have rested.

nodes.speaker: Katrina
nodes.text: I’m glad you found it. It has history that cannot be bought in a shop, however much I pretended otherwise. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The fountain makes the whole commons feel like a meeting point, even when everyone is hurrying to class.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: I keep forgetting which building has the practice hall. The signs are clear; my memory is not.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: Orientation looks much calmer from a bench with a snack.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The lantern trail is easy to follow in daylight. At dusk, every tree starts looking like a landmark.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The forest threshold is close enough to campus that I can practise a spell and still hear the gate bell.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: If you find the brook overlook, listen before you cast. The quiet is part of the place.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: Someone moved the cushions again. I respect the commitment to rearranging the common room every afternoon.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The quickest route to a study group is usually following whoever is carrying three books and a snack.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: I heard a Spellio match decided by one tiny turn. Games here are apparently serious research.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The commons is the only place where every route across campus seems to cross at once.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The orientation terrace is busy today. I hope someone remembered the schedule.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: Lanterns make the forest trail look welcoming, even when the woods are being dramatic.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: I saw a new trail marker near the clearing. Or perhaps I saw the old one from a different angle.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: The common room is quiet for almost five minutes after breakfast. It is a remarkable campus record.

nodes.speaker: Student
nodes.text: A good study plan includes a break, a second break, and finding out what everyone else is playing.
